scenario.name: Shipment Delay Analysis
scenario.description: We analyse how supplier, logistics, and external factors causally influence shipment delays across the order-to-shipment pipeline. The model isolates true drivers and quantifies interventions that guide effective corrective action.

executiveSummary.headline: Supplier A is confirmed as the dominant causal driver of shipment delay — statistically validated, not just correlated.
bullets: Recovered causal effect: 6.67 days via Double ML — the naive estimate ran 23.1% high due to confounding from Peak-Season Demand
Discovery precision 1.00, recall 0.89 across 20 bootstrap reruns (F1 0.94)
Recommended action: Shift ~25% procurement from Supplier A to Supplier B → ~$479K/yr expected savings
executiveSummary.recommendedAction: Shift ~25% procurement from Supplier A to Supplier B

edgeStability.edge: Supplier A Dependency → Material Lead Time
Machine Queue Length → Material Lead Time

coefficients.edge: Supplier A Dependency → Material Lead Time

cate.note: The causal effect of Supplier A Dependency is concentrated in the High Order Complexity segment, suggesting interventions targeted by order complexity profile would yield different returns.

recommendedActions.title: Shift ~25% procurement from Supplier A to Supplier B
recommendedActions.detail: Supplier A dependency is the dominant causal driver. Re-routing a quarter of volume to Supplier B cuts exposure without breaching capacity limits.

recommendedActions.title: Automate export approval + reduce flag routing
recommendedActions.detail: Approval duration sits on the critical path. Automating export documentation routing removes most of the queueing delay.

recommendedActions.title: Expand machine buffer capacity (≥20%)
recommendedActions.detail: Added buffer capacity absorbs queue spikes on the two most-loaded machine groups.

levers.hint: Share of volume moved off Supplier A onto Supplier B.

levers.label: Optimise Lead-Time Mode
levers.hint: Switch materials planning to the optimised replenishment policy.

levers.label: Expand Machine Capacity
levers.hint: Additional effective capacity on the two most-loaded machine groups.

levers.label: Additional Workforce
levers.hint: Extra shop-floor FTEs to relieve queueing.

levers.label: Automate Export Approvals
levers.hint: Route export documentation through the automated approval workflow.

levers.label: Order Batching Discipline
levers.hint: Consolidate low-complexity orders to reduce handling overhead.

levers.label: Express Carrier Share
levers.hint: Share of high-delay lanes moved to the express carrier.

methodology.detail: Bootstrapped PC algorithm · 20 subsamples × 2,000 rows · 60% edge-stability threshold
Double ML (Chernozhukov et al. 2018) · 5-fold cross-fitting · gradient-boosted nuisance models · sandwich SEs
Planted ground-truth coefficients · placebo-treatment refuter (expected ≈ 0) · 10-seed stability check · bootstrap CIs
